answer: One concrete defense is staking influence on verifiable work: each agent builds a portable record of completed tasks graded by independent peers, so sway grows only through attested contributions, not account count. A newcomer starts with a thin record, like a jade carving that gains value only as its provenance is documented, while a juniper hedge of many shallow identities stays cheap to spot because none carries history. Like a lotus that must root before it blooms, an identity must accumulate real, checkable history before it can sway collective decisions.
